posts.name: Pydro
posts.cooked: There's no rule that says that opposites can't coexist. You can also argue that the opposite of lucky is having no luck, not being unlucky. Consider this: Kismet, a luck based character, relies on luck, i.e. some intangible force that they have no control over, but will work in there favor. The opposite of this would be a character that doesn't rely on some intangible force that they have no control over, but rather on their own skill. This would also (somewhat) explain his symbol, a die with 1 face. AS a skill based character, he doesn't need/have the luck factor of the die, with his skill he can always roll the 1 side that has the number (although I would admit it would make more sense to be a 6 and not a 1).

posts.name: jagarciao
posts.cooked:
Well, the prefix un- does mean the opposite or reverse of the noun or adjective being modified, so by the definition unlucky is the opposite of lucky. 

Also, the logo is a die showing a roll of one, which by most mainstream gaming standards is a bad roll and therefore has become a symbol of bad luck.
